environment: Linux x86_64, Node 26.13.1, pnpm 10.32.1, PostgreSQL 16, Valkey 8, Chromium Playwright

limitations: isolated representative Phase 1 historical-guest upgrade, fresh schema and 99 anonymous participants
builds and records candidate images; no live promotion

commands.command: helm lint charts/application with explicit isolated profile values
helm template phase02 charts/application with explicit isolated profile values

limitations: Chromium isolated stack; no physical device run

acceptanceCases.expected: A fresh browser receives one confirmed anonymous cookie identity and joins as a durable user participant.
acceptanceCases.observed: Usage capture creates an anonymous identity and completes player-join/player-play against an isolated stack.

acceptanceCases.expected: Two delayed first tabs converge before join.
acceptanceCases.observed: Two independent session actors serialize the same Web Lock, recheck the native cookie, and create one anonymous identity.
limitations: deterministic unit lock, not a two-process browser worker

acceptanceCases.expected: Concurrent joins preserve one SQL membership.
acceptanceCases.observed: A partial unique SQL index on non-null party/user bindings and one transactional ensure operation preserve membership; P2002 maps to the active-claim result.

acceptanceCases.expected: One cookie works across GraphQL, media and Socket.IO while bearer/guest credentials fail.
acceptanceCases.observed: The isolated Chromium suite registers, requests recovery, logs in, uses GraphQL and realtime party routes with cookie authority.

acceptanceCases.expected: Anonymous cookies cannot perform account-only management actions.
acceptanceCases.observed: Registered management guards reject anonymous principals while anonymous party entry remains available only through the explicit player path.

acceptanceCases.expected: Transactional controller generation and takeover have one winner and reject stale handlers.
acceptanceCases.observed: Controller generations are durable and retirement increments the generation atomically with detachment; stale session registry checks reject old handlers.

acceptanceCases.expected: One active PLAYER claim is enforced while HOST-only membership remains independent.
acceptanceCases.observed: The unique user claim row is created after collision detection, released on leave/kick/retirement and skipped for HOST-only joins.

acceptanceCases.expected: Kick/leave/rejoin state transitions are durable.
acceptanceCases.observed: Leave/kick unit coverage and the full Chromium route/reconnect suite pass; statuses survive refresh through participants and claims.

acceptanceCases.expected: Logout, revocation and password reset revoke connected authority in ordering tests.
acceptanceCases.observed: Socket entry, observation, mutation and leave paths revalidate the native cookie at command time; browser revocation proves a second device loses authority.
limitations: password-reset ordering remains covered by the existing focused provider tests

acceptanceCases.expected: Account switch clears private state and ignores delayed callbacks/raw sockets.
acceptanceCases.observed: Sign-in revokes the previous native cookie session, clears scoped state, increments the frontend generation and forces realtime reconnect with the confirmed cookie.

acceptanceCases.expected: Private party reload uses membership without a password or guest token.
acceptanceCases.observed: Existing participant membership bypasses a password prompt and route recovery uses only the confirmed native user identity.

acceptanceCases.expected: Verified anonymous linking transfers ownership atomically and remains idempotent on retry.
acceptanceCases.observed: IdentityTransferService tests pass for transfer, collision rollback and completed-operation retry.
limitations: uses a transactional database double, not a crash-injected PostgreSQL run

acceptanceCases.expected: Active-party collisions reject rather than merge scores or create dual control.
acceptanceCases.observed: The transfer collision unit case rejects before ownership, score or session mutation.
limitations: not yet crash-tested on real PostgreSQL

acceptanceCases.expected: Native reset is generic, expiring, single-use and deliverable through SMTP.
acceptanceCases.observed: The browser suite completes the protected native recovery request; reset delivery remains native and verification records are bounded by maintenance.
limitations: external SMTP sink is intentionally not contacted by the isolated profile

acceptanceCases.expected: Account UI and protection pass in English and French.
acceptanceCases.observed: Full Playwright auth/session flows and generated English/French usage guides pass.

acceptanceCases.expected: Mobile/desktop reload and foreground recovery never mint replacement guests.
acceptanceCases.observed: Restore checks the native cookie only, all network failures retain the prior state, and browser refresh never reclaims a detached participant.
limitations: Chromium desktop/narrow viewport evidence, no physical device

acceptanceCases.expected: Migration upgrade, repeat, interruption, backup and rollback preserve representative data.
acceptanceCases.observed: The Phase 1 schema receives a representative registered host, historical-only guest and score, then the Phase 2 migration proves one detached participant, one preserved score and zero guest auth users; the normal suite reruns the same checked-in migration on a fresh database.
limitations: backup transport rehearsal is covered by the release/restore profile, not a live restore

acceptanceCases.expected: No live JWT/guest credential verifier or browser secret persistence remains.
acceptanceCases.observed: Old auth verifiers, GraphQL token mutations, Passport/JWT packages, token claims parser, and browser credential writes were deleted; focused scans only retain negative test fixtures.

acceptanceCases.expected: Expired auth users and sessions disappear while detached participant and score history survive.
acceptanceCases.observed: Real PostgreSQL retirement deletes the anonymous User and Session, nulls participant userId, preserves the score row and keeps KICKED/LEFT state.

acceptanceCases.expected: An unexpired native session blocks cleanup under real create/refresh/retirement ordering.
acceptanceCases.observed: The worker rechecks native session rows under locks and the valid-session PostgreSQL fixture remains intact; Better Auth write hooks reject committed retirement state.
limitations: uses the real schema and native hooks; a paused native callback is not part of the isolated suite

acceptanceCases.expected: An expired guest in a live party becomes LEFT/IDENTITY_EXPIRED or preserves KICKED and can no longer mutate.
acceptanceCases.observed: The worker expires an active participant, releases its claim/control generation, detaches it and leaves party/history rows present; sockets revalidate each command.

acceptanceCases.expected: Prepared and verified transfer deadlines are finite and terminal evidence does not pin users.
acceptanceCases.observed: The worker terminalizes PREPARED at one hour and VERIFIED work at 24 hours as EXPIRED/EXPIRED_PARTIAL while preserving deadlines and committed effects.

acceptanceCases.expected: Successful linking revokes source authority and makes it retirement-eligible.
acceptanceCases.observed: Identity transfer moves participant bindings, revokes all source sessions and enqueues source retirement in the same server transaction ordering.

acceptanceCases.expected: Startup/15-minute cleanup handles 99% anonymous churn in bounded PostgreSQL batches.
acceptanceCases.observed: The isolated real-database cohort retires 99 anonymous identities in one bounded sweep, retains 99 detached participants and keeps the single registered host.
limitations: accelerated synthetic cohort on the release runner, not a production traffic forecast

acceptanceCases.expected: Historical-only guests migrate as detached participants with zero auth users created.
acceptanceCases.observed: The dedicated pre-Phase-2 schema rehearsal converts one historical guest score to one nullable participant binding while the User count remains one registered host.

acceptanceCases.expected: A fresh identity cannot reclaim detached historical participants.
acceptanceCases.observed: The browser-held guest recovery port and all detached-ID join/rejoin paths were deleted; historical participant IDs are observation-only.

migration: The seven checked-in migrations deploy to fresh PostgreSQL. A separate schema first receives the first six migrations and a representative historical-only guest, then the Phase 02 migration reconciles one detached participant, one preserved score and one registered User.
rollbackRehearsal: coordinated image/database rollback remains a release-profile rehearsal, not a live operation
